```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

sheepdog checks whether the detections of a 'BirdNET' custom classifier are
real. Its first stage, covered here, builds a set of clips for manual review
from the BirdNET selection tables and summarises the verdicts of the
reviewers. Calibration (stage 2) and community matrices (stage 3) are covered
in other articles (see [Where next](#where-next)).

```{r}
library(sheepdog)
```

## Example data

The package ships a small simulated data set: BirdNET selection tables
(Raven format) of several sites recorded from October 2021 to March 2022,
with predictions of a custom classifier for anuran species. False-positive rates vary among species and sites, and the
confidence scores of false positives overlap those of true detections. The
generator is `data-raw/make_example_data.R` in the source repository. The
`Begin Path` column points to recordings on a fictitious network drive
(`N:\pam\audio\...`); the audio files themselves are not distributed.

```{r}
ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog")
list.files(file.path(ex, "birdnet"), recursive = TRUE)
```

## Reading the selection tables

`read_selection_tables()` finds every selection table under a folder, reads
them and stacks them. The site is taken from the name of the folder that
holds each table, and the column names are standardised (e.g.
`Begin Time (s)` becomes `begin_time`).

```{r}
det <- read_selection_tables(file.path(ex, "birdnet"))
det |>
  dplyr::select(site, species_code, confidence, begin_path, file_offset) |>
  head()
dplyr::count(det, site)
dplyr::count(det, species_code)
```

The tables hold `r nrow(det)` predictions of
`r dplyr::n_distinct(det$species_code)` species at
`r dplyr::n_distinct(det$site)` sites
(`r paste(sort(unique(det$site)), collapse = ", ")`).

## Selecting the clips to review

`select_clips()` applies the sampling design to the predictions and returns
the clip manifest, one row per clip to cut. It reads and writes no audio. The
default `"top"` design keeps the `n_top` predictions with the highest
confidence per site x species x night x hour; `max_per_species` then caps
the number of clips per site x species, drawing across the hours of the
night (`balance_by_hour = TRUE`). Because the hour window below crosses
midnight, recordings made after midnight are assigned to the night before.

```{r}
n_max <- 40
man <- select_clips(det,
                    sampling_mode   = "top",
                    n_top           = 2,
                    hour_start      = 18, hour_end = 2,
                    max_per_species = n_max)
dplyr::count(man, site, species_folder) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = site, values_from = n)
```

The manifest has `r nrow(man)` clips.

The `"top"` design serves classifier retraining and the score-to-probability
calibration of stage 2. It should not be used to estimate false-positive
rates, because top-score clips hold fewer false positives than a random
sample; the random designs are described in `vignette("sampling-designs")`.

The manifest links each clip to its source recording. Its columns are
defined in `vignette("crywolf-integration")`.

```{r}
dplyr::glimpse(man)
```

The columns used below are `species_folder` (the folder of each species in
the review), `night`, `confidence`, `clip_file` (the name of the clip,
unique within the run), and `source_audio` with `clip_start` and
`clip_end` (where the clip is cut from).

## Cutting the clips

`cut_clips()` cuts each clip of the manifest into
`<output_dir>/clips/<species_folder>/`, and `extract_validation_clips()`
runs reading, selection and cutting in one call, writing
`clip_manifest.csv` and one zip file per species. Both need the source
recordings and the 'av' package, so they are not run here. With real data,
check the selection first with `simulate = TRUE`, and remap the paths of the
recordings with `remap_from` and `remap_to` when the drive is mounted
elsewhere:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
extract_validation_clips("N:/pam/birdnet", "N:/pam/validation",
                         max_per_species = 40,
                         remap_from = "N:/", remap_to = "/Volumes/pam/",
                         simulate = TRUE)
```

## The manual review (simulated)

In real use, reviewers listen to the clips in the Review tab of the BirdNET
GUI (<https://birdnet-team.github.io/BirdNET-Analyzer/stable/usage/gui.html>),
which moves each clip into a `Positive` or `Negative` subfolder of its
species folder. sheepdog reads the verdict from that folder structure.

To make this vignette runnable, the review is replaced by a stand-in: each
clip is declared positive with probability equal to its confidence score,
and an empty `.wav` file with the name of the clip is created in the
corresponding subfolder of a temporary directory. These verdicts are
illustrative only; they are not the simulated truth of the example data,
and they assume a perfect calibration that real classifiers do not have.

```{r}
review_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "sheepdog-review", "clips")

set.seed(1)
verdict <- ifelse(stats::runif(nrow(man)) < man$confidence,
                  "Positive", "Negative")
paths <- file.path(review_dir, man$species_folder, verdict, man$clip_file)
invisible(lapply(unique(dirname(paths)), dir.create,
                 recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE))
invisible(file.create(paths))

list.dirs(review_dir, full.names = FALSE)
```

## Summarising the review

`classify_review()` joins the verdict found in the review folder to the
manifest. Clips left in the species folder are flagged `"not_reviewed"`, and
clips that are not found at all are flagged `"clip_missing"`.

```{r}
val <- classify_review(man, review_dir)
dplyr::count(val, species_folder, verdict)
```

`precision_by_bin()` gives the share of positive verdicts by site, species
and confidence bin. Bins with fewer than `min_n` reviewed clips are flagged
in `low_support`.

```{r}
prec <- precision_by_bin(val, min_n = 15)
head(prec, 10)
```

`suggest_thresholds()` returns, for each site and species, the lowest
confidence at which the precision among the clips at or above it reaches
`target_precision`, with at least `min_n` clips. `NA` means that no cut
reached the target with the clips reviewed. With at most `r n_max` clips per site x
species, many cells lack the support to reach the target;
`vignette("validation-effort")` discusses how many clips are needed.

```{r}
suggest_thresholds(val, target_precision = 0.90, min_n = 15)
```

`nightly_presence()` summarises the verdicts by site, species and night: a
night is `"confirmed"` when at least one clip is positive.

```{r}
pres <- nightly_presence(val)
head(pres)
dplyr::count(pres, species_folder, presence)
```

`plot_precision()` draws the precision curve of each species, with the
target precision as a dashed line and bins with low support faded. It needs
'ggplot2'. With several sites, each site is drawn as a line of its own
colour within the species panels.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), fig.width = 8, fig.height = 8, out.width = "100%"}
plot_precision(prec, target_precision = 0.90, min_n = 15)
```

`retraining_clips()` lists the positive clips for retraining the classifier.
With real data, `post_validation()` runs all of the above in one call and
writes each table to a CSV file, together with the figure.

## Where next

- `vignette("sampling-designs")`: choosing between the `"top"`,
  `"random_detections"` and `"random_recordings"` designs, the inclusion
  probabilities they record, and limits on the review effort.
- `vignette("validation-effort")`: how many clips to validate, from the
  curve of `calibration_effort()` and the support of each site x species
  cell in `precision_by_bin()` and `suggest_thresholds()`.
- `vignette("calibration")`: calibrating confidence scores (stage 2): the
  candidate models, their cross-validated comparison, calibration curves,
  scoring of every detection and nightly detection histories (`p_min`, k).
- `vignette("community-matrices")`: from calibrated detections to
  community analyses (stage 3): `community_matrices()`, the `k_min` rule,
  the effort filter and ordinations with 'vegan'.
- `vignette("retraining")`: turning the reviewed clips into training
  folders for BirdNET-Analyzer, with an independent test set.
- `vignette("crywolf-integration")`: the clip manifest and validation
  tables as input to occupancy models with false positives.
- `vignette("frognet-workflow")`: the complete workflow as used in the
  FrogNet project.
